items.title: A Transdisciplinary Science of Information within the Organogram of Consciousness
items.summary: Information transcends the traditional disciplines of physics, psychology, cosmology, and biology, yet remains connected to them through Zero-Point Energy. Although the origins of space, time, and matter are known, the when and how of Information’s emergence remain elusive.

items.title: Quantum tomography of fermion pairs in e + e − collisions: Longitudinal beam polarization effects
items.summary: We present a quantum tomography study of fermion pair production at future $e^+e^-$ colliders, emphasizing how longitudinal beam polarization controls the two-qubit spin density matrix. We study the processes $e^+ e^- \to t\bar{t},\ e^+e^-\to μ^+μ^-$ and Bhabha scattering $e^+e^-\to e^+e^-$, representing the mass threshold behavior, the $Z$ pole resonance and the $s/t$-channel interplay.

items.title: Nambu’s Dynamics, Strings, and Gravitized Quantum Theory
items.summary: In this article, we present a new view on string theory that is rooted in quantum foundations extended to the domain of quantum gravity in the form of gravitized quantum theory, in which the canonical probability measure captured by the Born rule of quantum theory, turns out to be dynamical and contextual. We claim that this gravitization of quantum theory is the essence of string theory.

items.title: Body in memory: the role of bodily self-consciousness in episodic memory and autonoetic consciousness
items.summary: Episodic memory (EM) enables the conscious recollection of personally experienced events, including contextual features such as visual, auditory and emotional details. However, the role of bodily signals has been largely neglected in EM, although the observer's body provides a rich bodily context during the encoding, storage and recall of events, and has recently been associated with a bodily form of self-consciousness (bodily self-consciousness; BSC).

items.title: Mind your head: Entropic Brain, irruption theory and the intelligibility problem
items.summary: Abstract The entropic brain hypothesis (EBH) and irruption theory (IT) are two recent frameworks to investigate consciousness by examining neural entropy. While they differ in their theoretical commitments, both aim to advance neuroscientific investigations of consciousness without succumbing to the intelligibility problem: the impossibility for scientific inquiries to provide intelligible access to subjective experience.

items.title: 100 ± Δ t years of quantum uncertainty: From origins to modern insights
items.summary: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle is a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, marking a decisive departure from classical physics. Conceived almost a century ago through a thought experiment showing that measuring an electron's position inevitably disturbs its momentum, it began as a deceptively simple idea that sparked countless studies and grew into the rich research field it is today.

items.summary: Higher-order body representations, including representations of body shape and size, play an important role in maintaining perceptual constancy in touch. However, whether the development of these representations depends on early visual experience remains unclear.

items.title: Actualization and the Quantum Mechanical Universe: Dissolving the Gap
items.summary: The actualization gap—the apparent discontinuity between the classical probability distribution delivered by decoherence and the single definite outcome that appears in experience—has been treated in the foundations literature as an outstanding problem in the physics of quantum measurement. This paper argues that the gap is not a physical problem and admits no physical solution.

items.title: Does Total Knowledge Mute Emotion? A Thought Experiment using Large Language Models
items.summary: Abstract This paper examines whether comprehensive knowledge acquisition attenuates emotional experience through a thought experiment that uses large language models (LLMs). We propose that LLMs, which possess extensive propositional knowledge yet lack phenomenal consciousness, serve as philosophical instruments for isolating the knowledge variable from other cognitive attributes.

items.title: Virtual reality as a neural state-modulating technology: EEG complexity during VR gameplay versus VR gameplay viewing

items.summary: Since 2019, eighteen NSF Research Traineeship (NRT) awards in quantum information science and engineering (QISE) and adjacent fields have been funded, constituting the largest NSF-coordinated investment in graduate QISE training in the United States. Synthesizing lessons from our programs, we work through the central tensions that every QISE graduate program must negotiate: between depth in a home discipline and breadth across the field, between structured instruction and open-ended experiential and hands-on…

items.title: Opposite post-processing orders of fermionic horizon channels and their quantum-resource monotonicity
items.summary: Abstract Studies of relativistic quantum information in noninertial and black-hole settings often focus on specific input states and resource functionals, leaving the common origin of recurring monotonic trends in quantum resources and correlations unclear. In this work, we identify a common channel-ordering structure from the complementary exterior and interior reductions of the effective single-mode fermionic horizon transformation, representing the physically accessible and inaccessible sectors, respectively.

items.title: Teleportation of Logical Qubits using Lattice Surgery with Superconducting Circuits
items.summary: Demonstrating a quantum advantage when solving large-scale computational problems on a quantum computer requires the correction of errors that occur due to limitations in control accuracy and coherence. Using the concept of quantum error correction, fault-tolerant logical qubits can be realized and manipulated with logical single- and two-qubit gates.

items.title: Causality, determinism and predictability: Probing nature through classical and quantum eyes
items.summary: In this article, mainly focussed on students and interested readers, we discuss how the understanding of causality, determinism and predictability is transformed as we move from the classical world view to the quantum description. We first explain how determinism and predictability operate in classical dynamics and outline the notion of causality.

items.summary: Which quantum causal structures can account for observed spatiotemporal correlations without access to an intervention-complete description of the underlying process? In particular, can such correlations distinguish a temporal chain, a common cause, and a common effect?

items.title: Liquid Integrated Network as Candidate Substrate for Artificial Consciousness
items.summary: Whether artificial intelligence (AI) system allows for generating machine consciousness has been a “grand challenge” which however must be answered in this day and age. Most contemporary AI is implemented on large scale solid-state electronic hardware, whereas biological consciousness is supported by much smaller sized space within a fluid-rich brain.

items.summary: Tensor network states (TNS) provide a family of efficiently compressed approximations to physically relevant many-body quantum states. An important quantity that characterizes the computational resources required by a TNS is its bond dimension.

items.title: From nonlocal correlations to local symmetry breaking: Asymmetry dynamics of crosscap states
items.summary: Under unitary dynamics preserving a global symmetry, bipartite entanglement typically grows while an initially broken symmetry is locally restored. Here, we show that this conventional scenario can be reversed when symmetry-breaking coherence is initially encoded in long-range entanglement.

items.title: Modeling quantum information scrambling in realistic protein NMR experiments
items.summary: Out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) are important probes of operator spreading and information scrambling, and have recently been proposed as a means of extracting molecular structural information through nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). Realizing this potential requires accurate modeling of OTOCs in complex molecular environments within experimentally relevant settings.

items.title: Local interference algorithms for observables in large random circuits
items.summary: In quantum dynamics, it is generally believed that interference effects lead to a sign problem for classical Monte Carlo sampling methods, rendering sampling ineffective. In this paper we show that this is generically not the case for the task of simulating the evolution of observables in random instances of circuit dynamics.

items.title: Nonlinearity-preserving quantum simulation of flows in the early fault-tolerant regime
items.summary: Ensemble prediction of nonlinear dynamics propagates a probability density whose linear transport equation retains the nonlinear drift, but grid-dependent circuit costs leave end-to-end feasibility in early fault-tolerant quantum computing unresolved. We couple polynomial reduced-order models fitted by sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics to Walsh-synthesized Koopman-von Neumann (KvN) transport and surface-code resource estimation.

items.title: Performance analysis of a Rydberg atom THz radiometer concept
items.summary: THz receiver technology lies between electronics and photonics; as such, its implementation is not as mature. This warrants investigation into alternative THz receivers such as Rydberg atom sensors, which are highly susceptible to electric fields.

items.title: Quantum amplification with a linear quantum coupler
items.summary: Josephson parametric amplifiers (JPAs) are essential components for quantum-limited microwave measurement, but their dynamic range is often constrained by Kerr and other pump-induced nonlinear effects. In this work, we systematically study the performance of a parametric amplifier based on the linear inductive coupler (LINC).

items.title: Integral Tensor Isomorphism via Cubic Rings and Lattice Methods
items.summary: We prove that isomorphism of integral $2\times3\times3$ tensors under $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\times\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathbb{Z})\times\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ is decidable in bounded-error quantum polynomial time. For a tensor $T=(A,B)$ with nonzero determinant form $\det(xA-yB)$, we use the parametrization of Wood by balanced modules to reduce the isomorphism problem to principality tests for compatible lattices, and use the algorithms of Bley, Hofmann, and Johnston to solve this in BQP.

items.title: Quantum simulation of neutral-meson mixing and decay on a reprogrammable photonic processor
items.summary: Neutral mesons oscillate into their antiparticles while decaying, so their dynamics is generated by a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian which a quantum simulator restricted to unitary operations cannot implement directly. We propose a reprogrammable photonic processor that simulates this open-system evolution through dilation and analyze it at the circuit level.

items.title: Non-equilibrium topological order from Floquet anyon proliferation in the toric code
items.summary: We analyze the dynamics of Kitaev's toric code in Floquet quenches where the drive coherently creates and propagates fermionic $f$ anyons. We show that the long-time state departs from pure-state topological order but retains long-range entanglement, thereby realizing a Floquet analog of intrinsic mixed-state topological order.

items.title: Optimal Min-Entropy Estimation with High Probability
items.summary: Min-entropy plays a fundamental role in assessing the unpredictability of randomness sources. In particular, NIST SP 800-90B specifies min-entropy estimation as a key procedure for entropy sources used in cryptographic random bit generators, illustrating the practical importance of reliable min-entropy estimation.

items.title: Riemannian geometry and quantum gravity on trees
items.summary: We show that the tree graphs that admit a quantum Riemannian geometry (QRG) with a positive ratio metric are exactly the Dynkin graphs of finite type $A,D,E$ and affine type $\widetilde D,\widetilde E$. A metric in this context is an assignment of a nonzero real value to each arrow and positive ratio requires that the two directions on any edge have the same sign.

items.title: Performance of Fusion-Based Quantum Computing with Imperfect Photon Indistinguishability
items.summary: Fusion-based quantum computation (FBQC) is a promising route to fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing, connecting small entangled resource states through linear-optical fusion measurements. While logical encoding can substantially improve resilience to photon loss, whether these benefits extend to other noise remain an open question.

items.title: Unique continuation for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
items.summary: We prove a unique continuation property for eigenstates of the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian, viewed as functions of the electron configuration with values in the spin-photon space. The vector potential may lie in $L^6_\mathrm{loc}$, with its divergence, curl, and the scalar potential in $L^p_\mathrm{loc}$ for some $p>2$.

items.title: Frequency Multiplexing of Purcell-Enhanced Optically Coherent NV Centers
items.summary: Integrating optically coherent quantum emitters into nanophotonic structures is key to scalable quantum networks. Realizing them with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is hindered by the degradation of optical coherence accompanying nanofabrication.

items.title: PRISM: A Logical-Physical Boundary Compiler for Dual-Rail Qubits
items.summary: Quantum computers can encode each logical qubit across multiple physical degrees of freedom so that errors on the physical qubits can be detected or corrected. A compiler must then translate each logical gate into native instructions, and one gate can have several equivalent realizations that interact through different wires.

items.title: Variable-length MDI QKD under source imperfections and local randomization over horizontal links
items.summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) provides security guarantees that hold despite device imperfections and finite-size effects. We address these challenges in measurement-device-independent (MDI) QKD, combining its intrinsic untrusted detection with an imperfection model for Alice's and Bob's sources via fidelity bounds.

items.summary: Recent observations by the Event Horizon Telescope have revealed important electromagnetic information around the supermassive black holes $\text{M87}^*$ and $\text{Sgr A}^*$, providing experimental supports for investigating physics near the event horizon. In the absence of a complete quantum gravity theory, exploring the observational appearances and polarized images of accretion flows in regularized geometries, and seeking specific observational differences from Kerr black holes, is of value for understanding…

items.title: Dynamical Decoupling via Continuous Unitary Design
items.summary: Dynamical decoupling is a cornerstone of quantum control for protecting and engineering quantum systems. However, conventional schemes rely on idealized instantaneous pulses, limiting their performance under realistic finite-duration and imperfect controls.

items.title: Non-Invertible Quantum Cellular Automata I: Microscopic Definition of Non-Invertible Symmetries
items.summary: We introduce non-invertible quantum cellular automata (QCAs), defined as locality-preserving quantum channels that are dualizable and pure. This provides an operator-algebraic definition of non-invertible symmetries of quantum lattice systems, formulated in terms of their action on local operators.

items.title: Problem-adjusted $X$-mixer eigenstates for improved QAOA
items.summary: We show that the use of problem-adjusted excited eigenstates of the $X$-mixer Hamiltonian can be beneficial for the performance of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) when applied to problems with degenerate ground states. We show that this advantage persists in the presence of quantum gate and readout noise, with the problem-adjusted excited initial states achieving better optimal performance than the standard ground state initialization.

items.title: Entanglement cost and classical capacity of multimode Gaussian states and channels
items.summary: Gaussian states and operations are central to continuous-variable quantum information and communication. For systems with any finite number of modes, we prove that entanglement of formation, Gaussian entanglement of formation, and entanglement cost coincide for every finite-energy bipartite Gaussian state.

items.title: Development of a Discrete Variable Representation of a Field-Adaptive Hermite Basis for Accurate Modeling of Magnetically Confined Systems
items.summary: Accurate magnetic-field evolution of spectra requires a common wavefunction representation that consistently describes multiple states across different field regimes. Discrete Variable Representation (DVR) methods combine accurate basis-based kinetic-energy evaluation with flexible real-space potential representation, enabling arbitrary non-analytic potentials to be treated.

items.title: Exact classical bounds of bipartite correlation Bell inequalities using improved branch-and-bound
items.summary: We present an improved branch-and-bound (IBB) algorithm for the exact computation of classical (local) bounds of bipartite correlation Bell inequalities. We strengthen pruning in the standard BB algorithm in two ways: a heuristic search based on see-saw iteration supplies a strong initial lower bound, and greedy row reordering of the Bell matrix reduces the tail bounds used during the exact search.

items.title: Molecular energies from sparse quantum prolate diagonalization on a trapped-ion quantum processor
items.summary: We introduce sparse quantum prolate diagonalization (sparse QPD), which combines the original formulation of QPD [Phys. Rev. Res., 8(3), 033177, (2026)] with compressed sensing to exploit Hamiltonian spectrum sparsity for molecular systems.

items.title: Oblique incidence and non-commuting limits: a remark on the convergence of Fresnel integrals
items.summary: The Gaussian integrals of quantum mechanics and of paraxial optics are oscillatory and only conditionally convergent. Textbooks usually make them converge by adding a small imaginary part to the time or by analytic continuation.

items.title: Depth-Dependent Collapse and Warm-Start Limits of a Symmetry-Preserving VQE for the J$_1$--J$_2$ Heisenberg Ring
items.summary: Increasing circuit depth is expected to improve a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). We show that this expectation can fail, and that curing the failure does not guarantee the exact ground state.

items.title: How can every physicist become a Bohmian
items.summary: The Bohmian interpretation of quantum mechanics is controversial because it attributes deterministic trajectories to microscopic particles. We propose a reformulation that sidesteps this controversy: rather than applying Bohmian mechanics at the microscopic level, we recast it as an effective deterministic description of the macroscopic pointer of a measuring apparatus, with no claims about the fundamental nature of the microscopic world.

items.title: Time-Travel Paradox in a Bohmian Extension of Deutsch's Approach: Mandatory Tunneling as the "Banana Peel Mechanism"
items.summary: We consider a self-prevention paradox in which a particle travels through a wormhole into its own past, encounters its younger version, and blocks its movement. In a specially constructed one-dimensional model, this collision rules out a classically self-consistent history.

items.title: Quantum-classical dynamical density functional theory for solvation dynamics
items.summary: We provide a unified modeling framework for thermalization and non-equilibrium spectroscopy in overdamped polar environments. This framework extends dynamical density functional theory to describe the coupled quantum-classical evolution of a molecular electronic subsystem and an overdamped polar solvent represented by a reaction-field coordinate.

items.title: Double-Bracket Quantum Algorithms for Preparing Multiple Excited States
items.summary: Many problems in quantum chemistry, many-body physics, and optimization require excited states of a Hamiltonian. Double-bracket quantum algorithms compile circuits recursively from evolutions under the Hamiltonian and a second operator, without a parameterized ansatz.

items.title: Finite-key security of BB84 with passive receivers via reduction to active measurements
items.summary: In BB84 with passive receiver basis choice (passive BB84) and threshold detectors, the distribution of detection bases can depend on the incoming photon number. Its relation to BB84 with active receiver basis choice (active BB84), in which the basis is chosen using independent randomness, is therefore nontrivial.

items.title: Catalytic imaginarity transformations
items.summary: State conversion is a central problem in quantum resource theories. In this work, we investigate catalytic state transformations within the resource theory of imaginarity.

items.title: The additive ambiguity of gravitational entropy fixed by the topology of the horizon
items.summary: In quantum gravity the algebra of observables of a subregion is of type III$_1$ at leading order in the semiclassical expansion, and it becomes of type II once the gravitational constraint is imposed. Hence generalized entropy acquires a trace, however it is defined only up to an additive constant.

items.title: An exact separability criterion for the $J/ψΛ$ spin state in $Λ_b^0\to J/ψ\,Λ$ decays at the LHC
items.summary: We derive an exact separability criterion for the spin state of the $J/ψΛ$ pair produced in $Λ_b^0\to J/ψ(\toμ^+μ^-)\,Λ(\to pπ^-)$ decays, taking into account the $Λ_b^0$ polarization at the LHC. Within the four-amplitude family $\{a_\pm,b_\pm\}$, the system is separable if and only if $(1+P_b\cosθ)a_+b_+=(1-P_b\cosθ)a_-b_-=P_b\sinθb_+b_-=0$, where $θ$ is the $Λ$ production angle defined in the LHC environment.

items.title: Tomographic reconstruction of non-Markovian Gaussian noise in continuous-variable photonic systems
items.summary: Memory effects in continuous-variable (CV) photonic systems can make standard Markovian Gaussian noise models inaccurate, even when the average noise strength is correctly calibrated. We propose a theoretical and simulation-based tomography framework for reconstructing such memory effects directly from time-resolved homodyne data.

items.title: Proven optimality for LABS with quantum-classical branch and bound
items.summary: Low autocorrelation binary sequences (LABS) are the phase codes of pulse compression radar and the synchronization words of digital communication, and finding the sequence of a given length whose aperiodic autocorrelations have the smallest sum of squares is a hard binary optimization problem. The quantum optimization methods tested on LABS so far return good sequences, but they cannot show that a sequence is optimal or bound how far from optimal it may be.

items.title: Complex quasiprobabilities as measurable temporal interference
items.summary: Quantum dynamics can encode interference information that conventional correlation functions leave unresolved. Here we show that the imaginary component of the extended Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability reveals dynamical distinctions absent from out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) formed from two repeated Hermitian observables at infinite temperature.

items.title: Resonance-induced quantum non-Gaussian states below criticality
items.summary: The Quantum Rabi Model (QRM), consisting of a single qubit coupled to a harmonic oscillator, provides a paradigmatic platform for exploring critical phenomena investigated for their applications in quantum technologies. In the superradiant phase of the QRM with coupling strength above the critical point, the bosonic ground state exhibits temporally stable quantum non-Gaussian features.

items.title: A Quantum Support Vector Regression Framework for Missing Data Imputation in Ship Performance Data
items.summary: The Internet of Ships enables vessels to generate vast amounts of data, yet missing values remain a persistent issue. To the best of the authors' knowledge, existing imputation techniques in this domain rely exclusively on classical machine learning.

items.title: Measurement-Conditioned Bloch-Sphere State Steering with a Continuous-Variable Pointer
items.summary: We investigate measurement-conditioned state steering of a qubit coupled to a continuous-variable pointer through a state-dependent displacement interaction. A position measurement on the pointer induces a nonunitary conditional transformation of the qubit, allowing its post-measurement state to move along a trajectory on the Bloch sphere.

items.title: Quantum speed limits from symmetries: A numerical analysis
items.summary: Target-specific quantum speed limits (QSLs) bound the minimal time required to realize a given operation. Recent theoretical work derives these limits directly from the symmetries of the dynamical Lie algebra of the control system and a symmetry-restoring perturbation, bypassing the need to solve the equations of motion.

items.title: Entanglement Lower Bounds for Symmetric Quantum Circuits
items.summary: Symmetric circuits require every symmetry of the input to extend to an automorphism of the circuit. In the classical setting, their connection to descriptive complexity yields strong unconditional lower bounds.

items.title: Quantum differential interference contrast microscope
items.summary: Optical sensing and imaging of transparent unstained biological and material specimen makes use of optical interference to translate phase shifts into intensity measurements, that are readily available in the optical domain. This is the case of Differential Interference Contrast (DIC) microscopes.

items.title: Local distinguishability of five six-partite orthogonal product states
items.summary: The local distinguishability of a set of orthogonal quantum states can be used to reduce the amount of quantum state transmission in quantum protocols and lower system operational costs and quantum resource overhead. In this paper, we investigate the local distinguishability of five six-partite orthogonal product states (OPSs), where any two states are orthogonal on only one subsystem.

items.title: Multilevel Effects and the Limits of the Quantum Rabi Model in Ultrastrong Coupling system
items.summary: The spectrum of artificial atoms coupled to resonators in the ultrastrong coupling regime have been analyzed using the quantum Rabi model over a wide range of coupling strengths. However, the accuracy of models obtained by truncating multilevel artificial atoms to two levels, as well as the correspondence between effective parameters extracted from spectral fitting and the bare parameters of the circuit Hamiltonian, depends on the multilevel structure of the system.

items.title: Quantum Codes for Distributed Quantum Fault Sensing
items.summary: Targeted recovery in modular quantum processors requires identifying the component affected by a fault. Independent qubits can monitor faults through repeated preparation and measurement.

items.title: Quantum Optimal Control of Many-Body States in an Antiferromagnetic XXZ Chain with a Single Local Magnetic Field
items.summary: We investigate the quantum optimal control of an antiferromagnetic XXZ spin chain with open boundary conditions, driven solely by a local time-dependent magnetic field applied to a single terminal spin. By optimizing the control field via Krotov's algorithm, we evaluate the feasibility of preparing multi-particle many-body states, including highly polarized Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ)-type states and study the mechanisms by which the control is applied.

items.title: Entanglement in restricted experimental setups
items.summary: Entanglement is a necessary resource for steering and Bell nonlocality, yet whether a state is separable takes no account of what an experiment can prepare or measure. We define two notions of separability relative to an experiment, one on either side of separability.

items.title: Anti-aging Squeezed Quantum Battery
items.summary: Exhibiting the superiority of energy storage and conversion over its classical counterpart, quantum battery (QB) emerges as a promising platform to revolutionize traditional energy technologies. However, their practical performance is severely constrained by the ubiquitous decoherence in microscopic world, which causes rapid aging and reduced ergotropy.

items.title: Analytical prediction of superradiant burst dynamics in extended atomic ensembles
items.summary: We present an open-system quantum theory of forward superradiant bursts in extended two-level atomic ensembles using coupled Heisenberg-Langevin and Maxwell propagation equations. Starting from a fully inverted state with zero mean polarization, local dipole correlations initiate emission without a prescribed tipping angle or stochastic seed.

items.title: Generating Massive Mechanical Superpositions through Qubit-Mediated Interference
items.summary: We propose a method towards demonstrating a quantum superposition of a massive mechanical resonator without the need for exact ground-state cooling, a requirement that becomes increasingly difficult to satisfy for low-frequency resonators. Our scheme relies on coupling the resonator to a spin-qubit.

items.title: Optimal Measurement Rounds for Perfect Encoded Fusion
items.summary: Encoded fusion combines probabilistic physical fusions to perform a logical Bell measurement. Adaptive choices depend on earlier measurement outcomes and therefore require multiple measurement rounds.

items.title: Strong eigenstate thermalization in Singer-cycle Clifford circuits
items.summary: Eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) provides a central framework for understanding thermalization in isolated quantum systems. Recently, the infinite-temperature ETH has been established for almost all Floquet eigenstates in linear feedback shift register quantum circuits.

items.title: Nonlinear function regression using quantum ensemble learning
items.summary: Recent advances in artificial intelligence and quantum technologies have driven the emergence of quantum machine learning, yet imperfections in near-term quantum devices remain a major obstacle for achieving practical quantum advantage. In the absence of fault-tolerant machines, ensemble learning, which combines multiple imperfect quantum devices, may unlock new quantum computing applications.

items.title: Zernike-efficient phase contrast with a scanned electron probe
items.summary: For weak-phase objects, scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) with a far-field detector transfers at most half of the phase information per electron that Zernike phase-contrast (ZPC) conventional transmission electron microscopy (CTEM) achieves. We propose APEX (Apex Phase-plate EXit-wave imaging), a scanned-probe mode that combines a defocused probe, a $π/2$ phase element in a magnified image of the probe crossover, and in-focus image-plane detection at each scan position.

items.title: Complex mobility edges from competing localization channels in non-Hermitian quasicrystals
items.summary: Non-Hermitian localization transitions often accompany multiple mobility edges, but their physical origin can be ambiguous. To address the issue, we introduce an extension of the Ganeshan-Pixley-Das Sarma model with both asymmetric hopping and complex onsite potential, thereby incorporating a broad range of non-Hermitian quasiperiodic chains.

items.title: Gradient Ascent Pulse Engineering for Multi-Time Correlations
items.summary: In quantum optimal control, gradient methods are often used to optimize functions of a state or propagator at a final time, while experimentally addressable observables and performance metrics may depend on multi-time correlations. We develop QRT-GRAPE, which combines the quantum regression theorem (QRT) with Gradient Ascent Pulse Engineering (GRAPE) to obtain analytic gradients for objective functions defined by multi-time correlations.

items.title: Quantum Interband-Coherence-Driven Inverse Faraday Effect in Intrinsic Graphene
items.summary: The inverse Faraday effect converts the angular momentum of circularly polarized light into a quasistatic magnetization, providing a fundamental route to ultrafast optical control of magnetic fields. We develop an analytical quantum theory of this effect in intrinsic graphene, where massless Dirac fermions, electron-hole symmetry, and weak spin-orbit coupling suppress conventional population-based interpretations.

items.title: Circuit compilation in the quspect quantum SDK: selecting routings after coupling-constrained resynthesis
items.summary: quspect is an open-source quantum computing SDK that provides circuit construction, C++ state-vector simulation with adjoint gradients, support for variational and combinatorial-optimization algorithms, Hamiltonian simulation, control-pulse envelopes and backends for several cloud quantum processors. Here we describe and evaluate its circuit compiler.

items.title: Logical error prediction and geometry selection for rectangular surface codes under biased circuit-level noise
items.summary: Realistic quantum hardware often exhibits biased noise, but at the circuit level this bias may affect only a subset of operations and need not be transferred uniformly to logical errors. The logical response to a given physical bias is therefore central to selecting resource-efficient surface code geometries.

items.title: CHEQ: A Concurrent Hardware Evaluation Platform for QEC Decoders via Batch-Invariant Circuit-Level Noise Sampling
items.summary: Hardware quantum error correction (QEC) decoders require validation of logical error suppression and timing compliance before deployment. Rare logical failures and deadline violations demand extensive sampling, while algorithm-level software evaluation does not directly measure hardware response times.

items.title: Context Has a Price: Adding and Removing Context for LLM Coding Agents under Prefix Caching
items.summary: Coding agents repeatedly send their conversation history to a language model. Adding useful code may reduce search, while removing old tool outputs may shorten later prompts.

items.title: MASQ: Measurement-Adaptive Sampling for Near-Clifford Quantum Error Correction Circuits
items.summary: Classical sampling of quantum error correction (QEC) circuits supports fault-tolerant protocol evaluation, but estimating rare logical failures requires many independent shots. Frame-active-state simulators isolate non-stabilizer information in a dense active-state vector, yet dense-state processing remains exponential in the active width.

items.title: Emergence and Persistence of Maximal Atom-Field Entanglement in the Jaynes-Cummings model
items.summary: We investigate the emergence and persistence of maximal entanglement between a two-level atom and a single-mode quantized electromagnetic field inside a cavity, whose dynamics are governed by the Jaynes-Cummings Hamiltonian. Using the von Neumann entropy as a measure of entanglement, we establish a direct connection between entanglement, atomic coherence, and atomic population inversion.

items.title: Symmetry-selected entanglement death at Floquet resonances of parametrically coupled qubits
items.summary: Periodic modulation of a qubit--qubit coupling is a standard way to engineer quantum interactions, but a strong modulation also reorganizes the transitions through which the qubits dissipate into a comb of Floquet channels. We study two identical, strongly coupled qubits whose transverse coupling is modulated anharmonically, as by a nonlinear coupler, with each qubit damped by its own reservoir.

items.title: Demonstration of a Qubit Control Scheme Compatible with Superconducting Digital Signals
items.summary: Superconducting quantum computing faces a critical scalability bottleneck arising from the escalating complexity of traditional analog control infrastructure. Single-Flux-Quantum(SFQ) systems operate at cryogenic temperatures and offer a potential route to addressing these challenges.

items.title: Exceptional-point Sensing with Quantum Advantage
items.summary: Exceptional-point sensors exploit singular non-Hermitian dynamics to enhance their response to weak perturbations. Recently, however, a no-go result has been established for a gain-loss-balanced dimer coupled to independent, phase-insensitive reservoirs: the exceptional-point susceptibility amplifies the signal and reservoir noise equally, precluding any quantum advantage.

items.title: Two-Qutrit Quantum Battery Charging through Ising Model and Anisotropic XZ Heisenberg Interactions
items.summary: In this paper, we propose a model of a two-qutrit quantum battery composed of two spin-1 systems coupled to an external field via anisotropic Heisenberg interactions. From the Ising model, we derive an exact analytical expression of ergotropy in the parallel-charging case.

items.title: Variational Relevance-Informed Sparsification of Term Measurements for Variational Quantum Algorithms
items.summary: Repeated measurements are a major bottleneck in variational quantum algorithms (VQAs). We uncover and characterize parameter-specific sparsity in the matrix of qubit-wise commuting (QWC) group contributions to parameter-shift gradients: most absolute contribution mass concentrates in a subset of groups whose relevance varies across parameters and optimization states.

items.title: Perturbative Recovery of Stabilizer-Subspace Correlations for Quantum Computational Chemistry
items.summary: Stabilizer-based subspace methods can substantially reduce the quantum resources required for electronic structure calculations, but the resulting projection neglects Hamiltonian couplings to configurations outside the retained subspace. In this work, we introduce Stabilizer-Subspace Perturbation Theory (SSPT) to recover the associated correlation contributions, using the Contextual Subspace Variational Quantum Eigensolver (CS-VQE) as a representative application.

items.title: Commutator-guided repair and classical-accessibility boundaries for shallow quantum circuits
items.summary: Trainability does not guarantee low-energy arrival: a shallow quantum circuit can be optimizable yet fail, under fixed depth and evaluation budgets, to reach Hamiltonian-selected states. We introduce a commutator-guided repair for this operational failure mode.

items.title: Electrostatic screening and nitrogen-vacancy charge states in boron-doped/nitrogen-doped diamond junctions
items.summary: Boron-doped diamond (BDD) enables the integration of electrical functionality with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers, but the influence of junction electrostatics on NV charge-state stability remains unclear. In this study, we investigate the equilibrium electrostatics of BDD/nitrogen-doped diamond junctions using self-consistent Poisson-Fermi calculations.

items.title: Analog-Memory-Based Waveform Generation for Qubit Control
items.summary: We propose an analog-memory-based arbitrary waveform generator for cryogenic qubit control that separates low-speed waveform programming from high-speed waveform generation. Waveform samples are stored as capacitor voltages and sequentially accessed through buffered switching networks, enabling repeated, non-destructive readout without high-speed digital-to-analog conversion.

items.title: Generative AI as epistemic technology and post-editing as a form of repair
items.summary: This paper examines how genAI-based translation technology challenges some of the conceptual foundations of TIS. In particular, it investigates the nature of genAI-based translation technology, the distinction between human cognitive translation capacities and machine operational capabilities, and the implications of this distinction for understanding post-editing and human–machine interaction in translation.

items.title: Connectivity from activity in spiking neural networks
items.summary: We show that a wide range of recurrent neural network models obey a simple set of equations tying synaptic connectivity and single-cell response properties to neural correlations. Our modeling framework considers networks in a stationary, asynchronous state and contains a broad class of synaptic filters, spiking nonlinearities, and random-plus-structured connectivity.

items.title: Pilot-waves and copilot-particles: A nonstochastic approach to objective wavefunction collapse
items.summary: We propose an extension to Schrödinger’s equation that incorporates macroscopic measurement-induced wavefunction collapse. We find that a hybrid between two leading approaches, the Bohm-de Broglie pilot-wave and objective collapse theories, accomplishes this goal in accordance with Born’s rule.

items.title: Squeezing and Decoherence of Axion Dark Matter
items.summary: Bosonic particles beyond the Standard Model, such as axions, are among the leading candidates for dark matter. If such particles have a small mass, they are usually described as a purely classical field.

items.title: Chronic hydrocephalus after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: a brain–CSF interface framework for mechanisms, conceptual states, and surgical management
items.summary: Chronic hydrocephalus following aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) may be more usefully conceptualized as the cumulative failure of several interacting brain–CSF boundaries than as a single obstructed conduit. A purely mechanical model cannot account for inflammatory CSF secretion, delayed absorptive failure, impaired clearance, altered tissue compliance, or the heterogeneous need for permanent shunting, so we use a brain–CSF interface and compartment framework to organize these observations.

items.title: Symmetric dilations of multi-qubit Pauli channels and semigroups
items.summary: We explore the symmetry properties of Stinespring dilations of single-qubit Pauli channels, addressing both the generic case and the specific examples of phase damping and depolarizing channels. For each scenario, we derive the representation of the Pauli group acting on the Hilbert space of the environment.

items.title: Observing Bell inequality violation beyond the qubit bound in a spinor Bose-Einstein condensate
items.summary: Correlations allowed by quantum mechanics can defy any classical explanation, with Bell nonlocality standing as their most profound and operationally powerful manifestation. While nonlocality has been demonstrated across a wide range of platforms, in many-body systems it has remained limited to ensembles of qubits, leaving the observation of higher-dimensional multipartite Bell correlations an open challenge.

items.title: The entangled loop: Emotion, interference and hierarchy in the architecture of consciousness
items.summary: Why does consciousness feel like something, and why is experience unified rather than fragmented? We propose that these properties arise from an entangled trefoil of emotion, interference-based inference and hierarchical orchestration, shaped by the thermodynamic constraint that living systems must remain far from equilibrium using limited energy.

items.title: Time-Division Multiplexing: The Operational Rhythm and Temporal Organization Layer of Digital Life
items.summary: Continual agents must handle urgent interaction while retaining alternatives, replaying errors, and committing safe long-term changes. A previous digital-life framework distinguishes online (busy) and offline (idle) channels, but leaves open whether these are separate programs or phases of a common process and how their operations should be ordered.

items.title: A systems-level energetic framework for conscious processing: energetic organization as a constraint on large-scale neural integration
items.summary: Conscious processing is associated with coordinated interactions among distributed neural systems, yet the biological constraints that enable and sustain large-scale neural integration remain incompletely understood. Contemporary theories emphasize computational, informational, and network mechanisms, while the potential contribution of systems-level energetic organization has received comparatively less explicit theoretical attention.

items.title: Multi-particle quantum walk search on a two-dimensional lattice
items.summary: In the present paper we study the formulation of a search problem and the efficiency of multi-particle quantum walk search algorithms. The discrete-time evolution of each particle in space is treated according to Grover's quantum walk evolution operator.

items.title: Residual Entanglement vs. Residual Coherence: A Wave Packet Approach in Neutrino Oscillation with Matter
items.summary: In this work, we investigate quantum correlations in three-flavor neutrino oscillations beyond the standard plane-wave (PW) description by employing a wave-packet formalism in the presence of constant matter density. We study three quantum correlation measures, namely the residual $l_1$-norm coherence, Concurrence Fill, and Three-$π$ entanglement, and express them in terms of transition probabilities for an initial muon-flavor state.

items.title: Attention Renders Sensory Contents into Conscious State via Content-invariant Frontal-Posterior Coupling in Humans
items.summary: Abstract Although attention promotes conscious perception, how it does so remains unclear. Human neuroimaging research has richly characterized attentional modulation upon visual processing, yet it remains unclear which of its components act as precursors of consciousness, which constitute consciousness itself, and which merely reflect post-perceptual, response-related operations.

items.title: OUCH: Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic Stimulation for Automated Neurological Assessment
items.summary: Motor responses evoked by noxious stimulation are used to assess neurological function in hospitalized patients with disorders of consciousness. In standard bedside assessments, these stimuli are applied manually, resulting in substantial variation in force, duration, frequency, and location.

items.title: Digital Minds: Issues in the Philosophy of Mind and Cognitive Science
items.summary: ABSTRACT This article provides a contemporary introduction to issues in the philosophy of mind and cognitive science that are studied within the emerging field of digital minds research. We explore the potential for AI systems to have mental states.

items.title: Local enhancement of finite-strength code preparation: recoverability and Wilson coherence
items.summary: Stabilizer measurements provide a direct route to preparing quantum error-correcting codes and long-range entangled states. In realistic implementations, however, finite measurement strength can coherently deform the encoding map away from the projective limit.

items.title: Probing chaos and criticality with observational entropy and finite-resolution measurements
items.summary: Coarse-grained measurements offer a scalable alternative to full state tomography for characterizing complex quantum dynamics. We show that observational entropy (OE), an information-theoretic entropy defined directly from finite-resolution measurement outcomes, provides a unified and experimentally accessible framework for quantifying chaos and probing criticality.

items.title: Quantum resources for everlasting communication security
items.summary: Abstract Quantum cryptography provides communication with everlasting security—a property unattainable by classical or post-quantum cryptography. Traditionally, quantum cryptography proclaims everlasting security by relying on principles such as no-cloning theorem, Bell inequalities, or the uncertainty principle, along with the standard assumption that legitimate users have no control over the communication channel.

items.title: The quantum-ready college: quantum technologies as an industry shift and how higher education should prepare
items.summary: Purpose This paper examines the emerging industry shift in which quantum technologies are evolving from isolated scientific breakthroughs into full-scale innovation ecosystems that will reshape higher education. Its purpose is to demonstrate why colleges must prepare now, well before fault tolerant quantum computers arrive, by developing quantum ready capacities across curriculum, workforce development, partnerships and cybersecurity.

items.title: Quantum Searching and Optimization Algorithms: A Comprehensive Guide
items.summary: This book offers a rigorous and forward-looking exploration of one of the most consequential frontiers in modern computation: the use of quantum mechanics to accelerate search, optimization, learning, simulation, and secure information processing. It begins by establishing the conceptual and mathematical foundations of quantum computation, including quantum gates, circuit design, quantum parallelism, and the distinctions between classical and quantum models of information processing.

items.title: Unitarity with respect to the clock of a dynamical local observer and the Einstein equivalence principle
items.summary: We investigate the unitarity of quantum evolution relative to an internal time defined by a local observer's clock. The observer is modeled as a relativistic particle carrying both a clock and a matter-field detector, analyzed first on a fixed curved background and subsequently within a fully diffeomorphism-invariant theory of dynamical gravity.

items.title: Pharmacokinetics of Local Anesthetics in Fascial Plane Blocks: Clinical Implications and Safety Considerations-A Narrative Review
items.summary: Fascial plane blocks (FPBs) are increasingly used in modern regional anaesthesia and differ from conventional nerve blocks by delivering local anesthetic (LA) into interfascial compartments. This approach results in distinct pharmacokinetics with clinically relevant systemic absorption.
